thread.title: Apple's stock bounces, but 'death cross' still likely this week - MarketWatch

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Apple's stock bounces, but 'death cross' still likely this week - MarketWatch
text:
Shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.33% bounced 0.9% in morning trade Monday, but that's not likely to stop the technology giant's price chart from flashing a bearish "death cross" pattern this week, which would be the first one seen since August 2015. The stock's 50-day moving average was at $197.8552, according to FactSet, and has been declining by an average of $1.07 a day this month, while the 200-day moving average is at $194.27 and falling by about 2 cents a day. At the current trajectories, the 50-DMA should cross below the 200-DMA on Friday. That would make Apple the fifth and final "FAANG" stock to produce a death cross, which many chart watchers believes marks the spot a shorter-term declines transitions to a longer-term downtrend. At Friday's 7 1/2-month closing low of $165.48, the stock had lost 28.7% from its Oct. 3 record close of $232.07. Of the other FAANG stocks , death crosses appeared for Facebook Inc. FB, -0.02% on Sept. 20, for Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, -1.88% on Dec. 12, for Netflix Inc. NFLX, +1.02% on Nov. 19 and for Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, +0.25% on Nov. 15. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite COMP, -0.05% flashed a death cross on Nov. 27, the S&P 500 SPX, -0.17% produced one on Dec. 7 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.23% is likely to produce one on Thursday.
